title: [VSC-6] VS Code client: wire parity with JetBrains (RELEASE_TASK, CHANNEL_DELETED)
description:
Epic epic-aabc654d (VS Code works + plugin reuse), sliced by task-a3e414a3 (VSC-0). First wave: no dependencies, files disjoint from the other first-wave rows. VSC-11 (Release Agent action) and VSC-12 (accounts wire) build on this row's MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Objective: the /ws diff in VSC-0's audit (882a4c39) found two messages JetBrains handles and VS Code does not:
1. RELEASE_TASK (outbound). JetBrains MoeCommandSender.releaseTask(taskId, reason?) sends `{ taskId, reason? }`, omitting reason when blank; the daemon handles it in packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts `case 'RELEASE_TASK'`. Add `releaseTask(taskId: string, reason?: string): boolean` to moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts on the existing sendMessage (false when not connected, like approveTask).
2. CHANNEL_DELETED (inbound; packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts emits it with the deleted ChatChannel as payload). JetBrains' MoeMessageDispatcher removes the channel; VS Code ignores the frame, so the chat view keeps a dead channel. Remove it from currentState.channels and tell the chat view (moe-vscode/src/providers/ChatViewProvider.ts already posts 'updateChannels' for CHANNELS; reuse that path or add an event). In moe-vscode/media/chat.js, an 'updateChannels' list that no longer holds the selected channel must stop selecting it (fall back to the first remaining channel, or none), instead of keeping currentChannel on a dead id.

Harness trap: seven test files transpile MoeDaemonClient.ts under node:vm, three with closed require maps (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness): add no value import. To drive the real client: `client['ws'] = { readyState: 1, send }`, `client['_connectionState'] = 'connected'`, feed `client['handleMessage'](JSON.stringify(frame))`, and JSON-parse sent frames in the test realm (vm-realm objects fail deepStrictEqual). chat.js runs raw in its own vm context (mem:pattern-vscode-webview-script-vm-test).

Not in scope: any Release button or confirm dialog (VSC-11), accounts messages (VSC-12), PINS_UPDATED and RESOURCE_UPDATED (neither client handles them; a JetBrains-first follow-up noted in VSC-0's doc), TaskDetailPanel.ts, package.json, extension.ts.

Verification (GLOBAL rail: never npm in the shared checkout): `git archive HEAD` of the whole repo into a fresh directory outside the checkout, overlay this task's files, then in <snapshot>/moe-vscode run `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` under `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mem:gotcha-vscode-gate-from-wsl). Baseline at 882a4c39: 388 tests, 384 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail.
definitionOfDone: New moe-vscode/tests/wire-parity.test.cjs drives the real transpiled MoeDaemonClient and asserts releaseTask('t1', 'Released from board') sends exactly one RELEASE_TASK frame whose payload is {taskId:'t1', reason:'Released from board'}, a blank reason omits the reason key, and when disconnected the call returns false and sends nothing.
The same test feeds a CHANNEL_DELETED frame and asserts the channel is gone from currentState.channels and the chat view is told once, while an unknown channel id changes nothing.
Running the raw media/chat.js in a node:vm context, an updateChannels list without the selected channel leaves the deleted channel neither listed nor selected.

Every existing suite that loads MoeDaemonClient.ts passes unchanged (daemon-identity, daemon-start, daemon-json-cap, plan-approval-client, protected-daemon-spawn, settings-wire, approval-paths, verified-local-launch).
In a git-archive snapshot of HEAD plus this diff, `cd moe-vscode && npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm run lint && npm run compile && npm test` exits 0 with 0 failures.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first. Create moe-vscode/tests/wire-parity.test.cjs with the Write tool (rail: no shell writes to tracked files). Use only node:test, node:assert/strict, node:vm, fs, path, net and typescript, which sibling tests already use, so there is no new dependency and no package.json edit. Read mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness, mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map and mem:pattern-vscode-webview-script-vm-test first.

HARNESS. Transpile src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and src/providers/ChatViewProvider.ts with ts.transpileModule (CommonJS, ES2020, esModuleInterop). Run each in its own vm.createContext with a closed require map that throws on any other name:
- client: vscode, ws, child_process, fs, path, net (as in tests/plan-approval-client.test.cjs);
- provider: vscode and path only. Its MoeDaemonClient import is type-only and transpiles away (architect-verified).
The vscode stub has:
- a recording EventEmitter (event/fire/dispose);
- window.createOutputChannel and showErrorMessage;
- workspace.getConfiguration() returning { get: () => false }, so no reconnect timer is armed;
- no workspaceFolders, so the STATE_SNAPSHOT path check is skipped;
- Uri.joinPath returning {}.
Connect the real client with client['ws'] = { readyState: 1, send, close }, where send records the frame first, and client['_connectionState'] = 'connected'. Feed frames with client['handleMessage'](JSON.stringify(frame)). JSON-parse every recorded frame and webview post in the test realm before deepStrictEqual, because vm-realm objects fail it. Dispose the provider and the client in finally.

SECTION A, RELEASE_TASK (DoD 1).
- A1: releaseTask('t1', 'Released from board') returns true and sends exactly one frame equal to {type:'RELEASE_TASK', payload:{taskId:'t1', reason:'Released from board'}}.
- A2: undefined, '', '   ' and a tab-plus-newline string each send payload {taskId:'t1'} with no reason key. A padded non-blank reason '  keep  ' is sent verbatim: JetBrains sends it untrimmed and the daemon trims.
- A3: the call returns false and sends nothing in three cases: _connectionState 'disconnected' with a recording socket installed; ws undefined; socket readyState 3 while the state says connected.

SECTION B, CHANNEL_DELETED through the real ChatViewProvider (DoD 2). Setup:
- deliver a STATE_SNAPSHOT {tasks:[], epics:[], workers:[], teams:[], proposals:[], decisions:[], channels:[general chan-g, custom chan-x]};
- construct new ChatViewProvider({}, client) and call resolveWebviewView with a fake view: visible; onDidDispose and onDidChangeVisibility returning disposables; webview {cspSource:'', asWebviewUri returning 'chat.js', postMessage recording a JSON copy, onDidReceiveMessage capturing the handler};
- send {type:'ready'} through the captured handler (the real handshake), then clear the post recorder.
Rows:
- B1: a CHANNEL_DELETED whose payload is the deleted ChatChannel {id:'chan-x', name:'x', type:'custom', linkedEntityId:null, createdAt} leaves currentState.channels ids ['chan-g']. The webview gets exactly one post, deepStrictEqual {type:'updateChannels', channels:[chan-g]}. The same frame again posts nothing more.
- B2: an unknown id leaves currentState.channels JSON-identical and posts nothing.
- B3, error handling: payloads null, {} and {id:42} change nothing, post nothing and do not throw. A client that never got a STATE_SNAPSHOT keeps currentState undefined and posts nothing.

SECTION C, the raw media/chat.js (DoD 3). Read it with fs and run it unmodified in a fresh vm.createContext per test. Stubs:
- acquireVsCodeApi() returns getState returning undefined, plus setState and postMessage that each record a JSON copy;
- document.getElementById memoizes one generic element per id: dataset, style, classList add/remove/toggle no-ops, addEventListener recording listeners by type, appendChild, querySelector returning null, querySelectorAll returning [], remove, scrollTo, focus;
- document.createElement returns a fresh generic element;
- window.addEventListener captures the 'message' handler (throw if none is registered).
channelTabs is a Proxy whose set trap empties the recorded tab list on ANY property write, because renderChannels clears the strip with one property write before it appends. The test never spells that property (project forbiddenPatterns). Helper listedIds() copies the current tabs, fires each tab's click listeners and returns the channel of each selectChannel post. Call it last, because a click changes the selection.
Rows:
- C1: updateChannels [chan-g, chan-x] auto-selects chan-g; then click chan-x's tab. After updateChannels [chan-g]: the last setState has currentChannel 'chan-g', the last selectChannel post is 'chan-g', exactly one tab's className contains 'active', and listedIds() is ['chan-g'].
- C2: with chan-x selected, updateChannels [] leaves currentChannel null in the last setState, zero tabs, chatInput.disabled and sendBtn.disabled true, and no selectChannel post after the update.
- C3, the guard: with chan-x selected, updateChannels [chan-g, chan-x, chan-y] adds no selectChannel post, and the last setState still says 'chan-x'.

Run it in place with `node --test moe-vscode/tests/wire-parity.test.cjs` (plain node, read-only; never npm in the shared checkout) and record the RED. Expected failures: A rows (releaseTask is not a function); B1 (chan-x stays, nothing posted); C1 and C2 (chan-x stays selected, input stays enabled). B2, B3 and C3 already pass.

implementationPlan.description:
Client half in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts. Add no import: seven harnesses transpile this file and three use closed require maps (mem:gotcha-vscode-vm-test-harness).

(a) After reopenTask, add releaseTask(taskId: string, reason?: string): boolean.
- Build const payload: { taskId: string; reason?: string } = { taskId }.
- Set payload.reason = reason only when typeof reason === 'string' && reason.trim().length > 0. Send it verbatim (untrimmed), as JetBrains MoeCommandSender.releaseTask does with isNullOrBlank.
- Return this.sendMessage('RELEASE_TASK', payload).
- Do not send force: JetBrains never does, and the Release button belongs to VSC-11.
- JSDoc: the daemon (WebSocketServer.ts case 'RELEASE_TASK') routes it through moe.release_task and substitutes 'Released from board' for a missing reason.

(b) Right after case 'CHANNELS' in handleMessage, add a braced case 'CHANNEL_DELETED':
- const state = this.state; const id = payload?.id;
- break unless state?.channels exists and id is a string;
- const remaining = state.channels.filter(c => c.id !== id); break when remaining.length === state.channels.length;
- then state.channels = remaining; this._onChannelsReceived.fire(remaining).
Write the state BEFORE firing; the opposite order is the TASK_UPDATED seam in mem:gotcha-vscode-notifier-seam-and-link-injection. Reuse the CHANNELS path: ChatViewProvider already posts {type:'updateChannels', channels} for onChannelsReceived. So ChatViewProvider.ts gets no edit, no EventEmitter is added and dispose() is unchanged. One comment line names the JetBrains MoeMessageDispatcher parity.

Error handling:
- A malformed payload, an unknown id, no snapshot yet or a snapshot without channels is a silent no-op: no event and no state write.
- handleMessage's outer try/catch stays the backstop.
- releaseTask inherits sendMessage's false when not connected, and its throwing-socket path (log, onError, reconnect, false).

Re-run `node --test moe-vscode/tests/wire-parity.test.cjs`: sections A and B pass.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: VS Code's MoeDaemonClient gains releaseTask(taskId, reason?). It sends RELEASE_TASK {taskId, reason?} exactly like JetBrains MoeCommandSender.releaseTask: the reason is left off when blank and sent verbatim otherwise. It returns false without sending when not connected. An inbound CHANNEL_DELETED removes that channel from currentState.channels and hands the chat view the pruned list once, through the existing CHANNELS path (ChatViewProvider posts updateChannels). The chat page drops a selection that is no longer listed. It falls back to the first remaining channel, or, when none remain, to its no-channel state (input disabled, empty-state text).
acceptanceCriteria: releaseTask('t1','Released from board') puts exactly one frame {type:'RELEASE_TASK',payload:{taskId:'t1',reason:'Released from board'}} on the socket and returns true.
A blank or missing reason sends {taskId} with no reason key. A disconnected client returns false and sends nothing.

CHANNEL_DELETED for a cached channel removes it from currentState.channels, and the chat webview receives exactly one updateChannels post without it. A repeat, an unknown id, a malformed payload or a pre-snapshot frame changes nothing and posts nothing.
Raw media/chat.js, given an updateChannels list without the selected channel, neither lists nor selects that channel. It selects the first remaining channel, or none when the list is empty.
invariants: MoeDaemonClient.ts gets no new value import. ChatViewProvider.ts and every existing moe-vscode test file stay unchanged.
The cached state is written before the chat view is notified.

The CHANNEL_DELETED payload is the deleted ChatChannel emitted by packages/moe-daemon/src/state/chatStore.ts; only payload.id is read.
onChannelsReceived keeps its meaning for its one subscriber (ChatViewProvider): the full current channel list.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
How the chat view learns about CHANNEL_DELETED:
(1) Fire _onStateChanged, like JetBrains publishState. Rejected: ChatViewProvider would also post updateWorkers, and the board, status bar, managed-VM tree and open panels would re-render for a chat-only change.
(2) A new onChannelDeleted event, plus a ChatViewProvider 'channelDeleted' post, plus a page handler. Rejected: it adds an emitter, a file and a second page path, while updateChannels has to handle a vanished selection anyway (a GET_CHANNELS refresh after a webview reload can drop a channel too).
(3) Chosen: fire the existing _onChannelsReceived with the pruned list, which ChatViewProvider already posts as updateChannels.
Not done: adding RELEASE_TASK/CHANNEL_DELETED to the types/moe.ts unions. handleMessage parses untyped JSON, isDaemonMessage has no caller, and types/moe.ts is VSC-8/VSC-12's file.
Unknown id: JetBrains publishes state anyway (a no-op filter). VS Code stays silent, so the DoD's 'changes nothing' is testable.
